preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 10,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 2 <= n <= 100000 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin_text.splitlines() if line.strip() and not any(c.isdigit() for c in line.split()[0] if c.isdigit())])
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is an integer between 2 and 100,000 inclusive.
The input describes a valid tree with n vertices and n-1 edges for each test case, and the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 200,000.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout_lines) == sum(1 + k for k in [int(stdout_lines[i]) for i in range(0, len(stdout_lines), 1) if i % 2 == 0])
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly k+1 lines per test case, where k is the integer printed on the first line of the test case output.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= x1 <= n and 1 <= y1 <= n and x1 != y1 and 1 <= x2 <= n and 1 <= y2 <= n and x2 != y2 for line in stdout_lines[1:] if line.strip() and (x1, y1, x2, y2) := [int(x) for x in line.split()])
postconditions.description: Each operation line contains four valid vertex indices where the removed edge endpoints are distinct and the added edge endpoints are distinct.
The sequence of operations transforms the initial tree into a bamboo (a path graph where every node has degree at most 2) using the minimum possible number of operations.
